meaning:
θνητός, -ή, -όν
(θνήσκω), [in LXX: Pro.3:13 20:24 (אָדָם), Job.30:23 (חַי), Isa.51:12 (מוּת), Wis.9:14 15:17, 2Ma.9:12, 3Ma.3:29 * ;]
subject to death, mortal: Rom.6:12 8:11, 1Co.15:53-54, 2Co.4:11 5:4.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Therefore don’t let sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts.
For this perishable body must become imperishable, and this mortal must put on immortality.
For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
